You are fixing three defects in ONE Python file's bio extraction. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY THREE FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py   (edit)
  2. tests/test_guest_email_context.py        (edit — extend, do not delete existing tests)
  3. fix-summary.md                           (create)

Touching any other file fails the check. Do NOT edit server/pipeline/guest_assets.py — it consumes this module and must keep working unchanged.

## Why this matters

This module extracts a guest's bio, headshot and links from their email so the prep document, show notes and on-air intro can use them. On 2026-08-11, for a real guest recording that day, its three bio candidates were: an email confidentiality footer, the show owner's own request (quoted in the guest's Outlook-style reply), and the owner's signature block — while the guest's actual professional bio, sitting in the same message, was rejected. A bio is read aloud on air and published under a real person's name; offering a legal footer as their biography is the worst thing this module can do.

## The three defects, proven by executed probes against live mail

D1 — lines ~19-22 define _FIRST_PERSON_RE and line ~355 REQUIRES it for every bio candidate. Professional bios are written in THIRD person ('Dana Kowalczyk, MBA, CEPA is a Certified Exit Planning Advisor...') and contain no first-person pronoun, so they are rejected — while conversational asks ('so we make you look good... I don't butcher it') and confidentiality footers ('we can ensure such a mistake') sail through. The filter is exactly backwards for this artifact.

D2 — _strip_quoted_reply (lines ~155-163) recognises only Gmail-style quoting: 'On ... wrote:' boundary lines and '>'-prefixed lines. Outlook clients quote with a '-----Original Message-----' line and/or a 'From: ... / Sent: ... / To: ... / Subject: ...' header block, with NO '>' prefixes. That history — the OWNER'S text — survives stripping and is attributed to the guest.

D3 — _is_full_body_extract rejects a candidate equal to the whole message body, so a reply whose entire body IS the bio (the cleanest possible response) produces nothing.

## The fix, in spirit

1. Strip Outlook history: in _strip_quoted_reply, ALSO stop at the first line matching '-----Original Message-----' (tolerant of dash count/spacing) or a 'From:' line that is followed within the next three lines by 'Sent:'/'To:'/'Subject:' lines (that lookahead protects a guest legitimately writing a paragraph that happens to start 'From:'). Everything from that boundary down is quoted history.

2. Replace the hard first-person requirement with an accept/reject pair:
   REJECT a paragraph as boilerplate when it matches legal/administrative signals — confidentiality/disclaimer language ('confidential', 'strictly forbidden', 'intended for the recipient', 'received this message by mistake', unsubscribe text) — or when it is a signature block (short lines dominated by name/title/phone/URL rather than sentences).
   ACCEPT a 25-120-word non-boilerplate paragraph when ANY of: (a) it matches _FIRST_PERSON_RE (unchanged behaviour), (b) it is third-person biographical — it contains a token of the GUEST'S OWN NAME (you have guest_email; derive name tokens from the From header of their messages, comparing case-insensitively) near a linking verb or credential pattern ('is a', 'serves', 'founded', 'MBA', 'OD', 'FAAO' and the like), or (c) it immediately follows a bio-cue paragraph (a preceding paragraph containing 'bio' used as a noun cue, e.g. "here's a quick bio").
   Do not over-engineer: precision matters more than recall, EXCEPT that the three watched-red scenarios must pass. When unsure, prefer rejecting an ambiguous paragraph over admitting boilerplate.

3. Fix D3 minimally: a body that IS a single qualifying bio paragraph is not a 'full-body extract' to discard — the full-body guard exists to avoid swallowing whole conversational emails, so keep it for paragraphs that do NOT independently qualify under rule 2, and let a qualifying paragraph through even when it is the entire body.

4. The guest's words are returned as found (the existing whitespace normalisation in _paragraphs is fine); never merge, trim or rewrite content beyond that existing normalisation.

Add tests to tests/test_guest_email_context.py mirroring the three defects (third-person bio accepted; Outlook history stripped; footer/signature rejected; bio-only body accepted; first-person still accepted). Keep every existing test passing — they encode current good behaviour for headshots, links, quotes and Gmail-style stripping.

## Run BOTH until each passes

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u21_guest_assets_check.py --worktree "$PWD"
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_guest_email_context.py tests/test_guest_assets.py -q

(If tests/test_guest_assets.py does not exist, run the guest-assets-related test file that does; name it in your summary.)

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of BOTH commands. Under 'Risk' name one message shape that could still defeat the extraction after this fix. Under 400 words.
